authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: INSW (the acquirer) completed its acquisition of Bruton Limited and its newbuilding VLCCs, paid mainly in INSW shares plus cash.
The Board declared a combined dividend of $5.05 per share, payable in the fourth quarter. It was declared but not yet paid as of the filing.
INSW sold a Suezmax in the third quarter, with net proceeds of $74 million and a gain of $53 million.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 business description
business_model.claim: International Seaways sells ocean transportation of crude oil and refined petroleum products, using a fleet of oceangoing tankers that operate in the International Flag market.
quotes: own and operate a fleet of oceangoing vessels engaged primarily in the transportation of crude oil and petroleum products in the International Flag trade.

business_model.claim: Its customers, including those reached through the commercial pools it joins, are oil companies, oil traders, refinery operators and government entities.
quotes: Our ultimate customers, including those of the commercial pools in which we participate, include major independent and state-owned oil companies, oil traders, refinery operators and international government entities.

business_model.basis: percentages are stated in the 10-Q MD&A; the explanation of the shift is inferred from the segment rate data in P7
business_model.claim: The business reports two segments, Crude Tankers and Product Carriers. Crude Tankers supplied 73% of TCE revenues in the third quarter of 2026 and 64% for the nine months, against 48% and 49% a year earlier, so the mix has moved strongly toward crude.
quotes: Our business includes two reportable segments: Crude Tankers and Product Carriers.
we derived 73% and 64%, respectively, of our time charter equivalent

business_model.basis: figures are stated in the 10-Q income statement; the description of each stream is inferred from the 10-K business text
business_model.claim: Shipping revenue comes from three arrangements: pool revenues, time and bareboat charter revenues, and voyage charter revenues. For the nine months to September 30, 2026, shipping revenues were 1,275,965 (table in thousands), made up of pool 719,574, time charter 263,605 and voyage charter 292,786. For the same period of 2025 the total was 575,423.

Revenue is mostly spot-market exposed. About 82% of TCE revenues came from the spot market in the latest annual period, against 86% the year before, mainly through commercial pools. A smaller part is fixed-rate time charter income.
quotes: We derived approximately 82% and 86% of our total TCE revenues in the spot market for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
Spot market rates are highly volatile, while time charter and bareboat charter rates provide more predictable streams of TCE revenues because they are fixed for specific periods of time.

business_model.basis: stated in the earnings release; the profit-share structure is described in the 10-K MD&A footnote
business_model.claim: Third-quarter 2026 time charter earnings were boosted by profit-sharing on top of the base rate. The release reports Crude Tankers time charter earnings of approximately $274,000 per day.
quotes: higher average time charter earnings of approximately $274,000 per day, reflecting higher profit-sharing results

business_model.claim: The main revenue driver is the freight rate set by tanker supply and demand, and geopolitical disruption has recently pushed rates sharply higher. Management says the Middle East war that began in late February 2026 raised spot charter rates, but it expects the current historically high levels not to last.
quotes: Rates for the transportation of crude oil and refined petroleum products from which the Company earns a substantial majority of its revenues are determined by market forces such as the supply and demand for oil
it is unlikely that the charter rates will remain at these historically high levels

business_model.basis: figures are stated in the statements; the cost mechanism is stated in the 10-Q and release, with part inferred
business_model.claim: Third-quarter 2026 shipping revenues were 483,202 (table in thousands) against 196,388 a year earlier, and voyage charter revenues rose to 153,690 from 11,325. Voyage expenses rose in step to 40,645 from 3,920, because under voyage charters the company bears the voyage costs. Management therefore judges performance by TCE revenues, defined as shipping revenues less voyage expenses.
quotes: the Company uses TCE revenues, which represents shipping revenues less voyage expenses

business_model.basis: figures are stated in the income statement; the leverage reading is inferred from comparing the lines
business_model.claim: The cost base is mostly vessel-related and changes little with freight rates: vessel expenses, charter hire for chartered-in ships, depreciation and amortization, and general and administrative. For the third quarter of 2026, vessel expenses were 64,051 against 65,815 a year earlier, while shipping revenues more than doubled, which shows strong operating leverage. Charter hire expenses rose to 21,214 from 7,134.

business_model.basis: figures are stated in the statements and release; the strategy is stated in the 10-K
business_model.claim: Selling vessels is a repeated part of earnings. Gains on disposal were 52,817 in the third quarter of 2026 against 13,658 a year earlier. Adjusted net income of 291,421, which excludes the gain, is below reported net income of 344,238.
quotes: Gain on disposal of vessels and other assets, net
actively manage the size, age and composition of our fleet over the course of market cycles

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and balance sheet
business_model.claim: The company is asset-heavy. At September 30, 2026 it ran an operating fleet of 65 owned, lease-financed or chartered vessels totaling 7.6 million deadweight tons. Vessels and other property net of depreciation stand at 2,104,268 (table in thousands), and long-term debt at 665,371.
quotes: consisted of 65 wholly-owned or lease financed vessels aggregating 7.6 million deadweight tons

business_model.basis: figures and the payout statement are stated in the cash flow statement and release
business_model.claim: Operating cash flow in the first nine months of 2026 was 651,755 (table in thousands), against 234,051 a year earlier. Most of it went to shareholders: cash dividends paid were 581,887. Management states a payout of at least 85% of adjusted net income for four consecutive quarters.
quotes: Fourth consecutive quarter with a payout ratio of at least 85% of adjusted net income.

competitive_position.claim: INSW is a large tanker owner-operator. At year-end 2025 it ran 70 vessels totalling 8.4 million dwt across crude tankers (VLCC, Suezmax, Aframax) and product carriers (LR2, LR1, MR).
quotes: we owned or operated an International Flag fleet of 70 vessels (totaling an aggregate of 8.4 million dwt)

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release; the comparison with 70 vessels is inferred across two filings.
competitive_position.claim: By September 30, 2026 the operating fleet was 65 vessels of 7.6 million dwt, with four LR1 newbuilds on order, for 69 in total. The count fell from year-end 2025 through vessel sales, and the fleet was also adding Bruton's VLCC newbuildings.
quotes: consisted of 65 wholly-owned or lease financed vessels aggregating 7.6 million deadweight tons

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A and Item 1.
competitive_position.claim: INSW's revenue is predominantly spot-market, earned through commercial pools. This gives strong upside when rates rise and volatility when they fall.
quotes: We derived approximately 82% and 86% of our total TCE revenues in the spot market for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

competitive_position.basis: Statement values are printed in the 10-Q; the cause is stated in management's comment.
competitive_position.claim: Third-quarter 2026 results show the earnings leverage of that position. Net income was 344,238 (table in thousands) against 70,546 a year earlier, on shipping revenues of 483,202 against 196,388. Management credits exceptional tanker market conditions as well as its capital allocation.
quotes: We delivered record quarterly net income, reflecting both exceptional tanker market conditions and the benefits of our long-term approach to fleet investment and capital allocation.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the earnings release and 10-Q MD&A; the table reading is inferred.
competitive_position.claim: Crude-tanker rates drove the quarter. Crude Tankers' average spot earnings were over $78,000 per day higher, and the VLCC spot rate was $154,597 against $34,809 a year earlier. Crude Tankers also rose to 73% of TCE revenues in the quarter from 48%.
quotes: higher average spot earnings of over $78,000 per day

competitive_position.basis: Statement figures are printed in the cash flow statement; the payout policy is stated in the earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: Cash generation is large and funds returns to shareholders. Nine-month operating cash flow was 651,755 (table in thousands) against 234,051, and dividends paid were 581,887 against 102,127.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the earnings release; debt comparison from the balance sheet.
competitive_position.claim: The balance sheet gives financial capacity to compete for assets. Liquidity was about $964 million at September 30, 2026, made up of $454 million of cash and short-term investments and $510 million of undrawn revolver capacity, and net loan-to-value was below 6%.
quotes: Total liquidity was approximately $964 million as of September 30, 2026, including cash and short-term investments of $454 million and $510 million undrawn revolving credit capacity.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and 8-Ks; the risk is from 10-K Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: INSW is expanding through acquisition. It agreed in October 2026 to acquire Bruton Limited, which brought four VLCC newbuildings, funded mainly with shares plus cash. Management says this uses its shares as currency for growth.
quotes: the Company executed a series of agreements to acquire Bruton Limited

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and 10-K Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: The main threat is normalisation of rates. The 10-Q says current charter rates are unlikely to stay at historically high levels, and the 10-K warns that normalisation of geopolitical conditions could cause tanker rates to decline significantly.
quotes: it is unlikely that the charter rates will remain at these historically high levels.
any such normalization could cause tanker rates to decline significantly

competitive_position.claim: Earnings are cyclical and product carriers have already weakened once. In 2025, Product Carriers TCE revenues fell 20% as lower daily rates offset fleet changes.
quotes: During 2025, TCE revenues for the Product Carriers segment decreased by $99.7 million, or 20%, to $396.3 million from $496.0 million in 2024.

competitive_position.claim: Fleet supply growth is a named threat. The tanker newbuilding order book was about 17% of the fleet at year-end 2025, up from 14% and 7% in the prior two year-ends, and new deliveries could raise capacity faster than demand.
quotes: equaled approximately 17%, 14% and 7% as of each of December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023

competitive_position.claim: Trade policy on port fees is a named risk. INSW owns 13 China-built vessels (four of them below the dwt minimum for U.S. fees) and may be subject to China's reciprocal fees on U.S.-controlled operators. Both countries have suspended their fee orders, but the extension is not finalised.
quotes: The Company currently owns 13 vessels that were constructed in China (four of which are below the 55,000 dwt minimum to which the U.S. fees apply)

financial_health.basis: Stated in the earnings release and the balance sheet; the year-end comparison is stated in the 10-K.
financial_health.claim: Liquidity is large against near-term obligations. The company reports total liquidity of approximately $964 million at the latest quarter-end, made up of $454 million of cash and short-term investments plus $510 million of undrawn revolver capacity. Current assets of 895,596 (table in thousands) compare with current liabilities of 133,853 (table in thousands). Year-end 2025 liquidity was $723.6 million.
quotes: Total liquidity was approximately $964 million as of September 30, 2026, including cash and short-term investments of $454 million and $510 million undrawn revolving credit capacity.

financial_health.basis: Balance sheet figures are stated; the loan-to-value ratios are company-reported in the release and the 10-K.
financial_health.claim: Reported debt rose over the nine months but leverage stays low. Long-term debt was 665,371 (table in thousands) against 541,291 at year-end, and current installments were 34,626 against 25,788. Total liabilities were 807,197 against total equity of 2,365,615. Management states net loan-to-value of less than 6%, against 12.9% at the end of 2025.
quotes: Net loan-to-value(1) less than 6% as of September 30, 2026.
Long-term debt | 665,371 | 541,291

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement and the earnings release.
financial_health.claim: Cash generation is very strong. Nine-month net cash from operating activities was 651,755 (table in thousands) against 234,051 a year earlier. The company reports quarterly free cash flow of $234 million, and nine-month adjusted EBITDA was 933,342 (table in thousands) against 299,909.
quotes: Net cash provided by operating activities | 651,755 | 234,051
Strong quarterly free cash flow(1) of $234 million.

financial_health.basis: Inferred from comparing the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement; the line items are stated.
financial_health.claim: Operating cash flow is lower than net income. Net income was 925,306 (table in thousands) against operating cash flow of 651,755. Two items explain much of the gap: a 204,028 increase in voyage receivables, and 140,945 of vessel sale gains that are deducted in operating activities because their proceeds sit in investing. Voyage receivables were 381,915 against 177,887 at year-end, of which unbilled were 273,872 against 169,610.
quotes: (Increase)/decrease in voyage receivables | (204,028) | 30,504

financial_health.basis: Management statement in the 10-Q; the spot-exposure point comes from the 10-K risk factors and the dependence is inferred.
financial_health.claim: The earnings and cash flow rest on an exceptional rate environment that management does not expect to last. The 10-Q says charter rates are historically high following the Middle East disruption, but that it is unlikely they remain at these levels. The company relies on spot-market exposure for most of its revenue.
quotes: it is unlikely that the charter rates will remain at these historically high levels

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement and the 8-K.
financial_health.claim: Shareholder distributions are the largest use of cash. Dividends paid were 581,887 (table in thousands) against 102,127, and net cash used in financing was 456,329. A further combined dividend of $5.05 per share is payable in the fourth quarter. Capital expenditure on vessels was 199,309, partly funded by 296,572 of disposal proceeds.
quotes: declared a combined dividend of $5.05 per share of common stock payable in the fourth quarter of 2026

financial_health.basis: Stated on the balance sheet and cash flow statement; the coverage is inferred by comparison.
financial_health.claim: Debt falling due within a year is small against cash. Current installments of long-term debt were 34,626 (table in thousands) against cash and cash equivalents of 163,627 and short-term investments of 290,000. During the nine months the company drew 127,000 on revolvers and repaid 127,000, and borrowed 158,245 on nonrevolving facilities.
quotes: Current installments of long-term debt | 34,626 | 25,788

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1; the maturity profile as a whole is not shown.
financial_health.claim: The one long-dated bullet maturity identified is a $250 million 7.125% senior unsecured bond due September 23, 2030, which does not amortise. The company also has an ECA facility for its LR1 newbuilds with a 12-year term and 20-year amortisation. The bond proceeds were used to buy out the Ocean Yield lease financing, which cut annual mandatory principal payments.
quotes: We issued $250 million aggregate principal amount of non-amortizing, 7.125% senior unsecured bonds maturing on September 23, 2030 at an issue price of 100%.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the 8-Ks; the effect on liquidity is inferred and not quantified.
financial_health.claim: The Bruton acquisition was agreed in October, after the quarter-end, so its effect on cash and debt is not in the balance sheet. The consideration is described as shares and cash, and the deal brings two VLCCs already built or delivering plus two newbuild VLCCs.
quotes: in October 2026, the Company executed a series of agreements to acquire Bruton Limited.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q income statement and the 10-Q MD&A. The causal link is the company's own explanation.
growth_thesis.claim: Much higher charter rates, tied to the Middle East war disruption, drove the jump in results. Third-quarter shipping revenues were 483,202 against 196,388 a year earlier, and net income was 344,238 against 70,546 (statements in thousands of dollars). For this to continue, rates must stay near current levels. Management itself says they are unlikely to.
quotes: it is unlikely that the charter rates will remain at these historically high levels

growth_thesis.basis: Rate figures are stated in the earnings release table. The spot share is stated in the 10-K risk factors. The link between the two is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Heavy spot-market exposure is the transmission channel. VLCC average spot TCE rate was $154,597 in the third quarter of 2026 against $34,809 a year earlier. Spot was 82% of TCE revenues in 2025. Earnings keep growing only if spot rates stay elevated, because the fleet is mostly unfixed.
quotes: In the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, INSW derived approximately 82%, 86% and 91%, respectively, of its TCE revenues in the spot market.

growth_thesis.basis: Acquisition and delivery schedule are stated in the 10-Q MD&A. Earnings contribution is inferred and not quantified in the evidence.
growth_thesis.claim: Fleet expansion through the Bruton acquisition adds crude capacity: four VLCC newbuildings, of which one dual-fuel unit is already operational. Growth from this requires the remaining units to be delivered on schedule and to find profitable employment in a still-strong crude market.
quotes: In conjunction with the Merger, the Company acquired two 2026-built, scrubber-fitted, dual-fuel (LNG) VLCC newbuildings and two scrubber-fitted VLCC newbuildings.

growth_thesis.basis: Order and pool statements are in the second-quarter release. The segment figures are in the third-quarter release. Continuation is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: A product-carrier newbuilding program, an extra four LR1s ordered at an aggregate $244 million, is a further capacity driver. It needs the LR1 pool to keep outperforming and the deliveries to arrive on time. Product Carriers segment TCE revenues were $121 million in the third quarter, up from $99 million.
quotes: Contracted four additional LR1 newbuildings for an aggregate price of $244 million, with deliveries expected in 2028.

growth_thesis.basis: Gain amounts are stated in the income statement and release. The dependence on vessel values is inferred from the 10-K risk factor on vessel values.
growth_thesis.claim: Vessel sales are a recurring contributor to reported profit. Gains on disposal were 140,945 for nine months against 34,908 a year earlier (thousands of dollars). Continued gains require sale prices to stay above carrying values. The third quarter included a Suezmax sale for $74 million net proceeds with a $53 million gain. The company's adjusted net income excludes these gains.
quotes: Sold a 2012-built Suezmax for proceeds, net of commissions and fees, of $74 million, recognizing a gain of $53 million.

growth_thesis.basis: Cash flow and liquidity are stated in the cited items. The retention and funding inference is the analyst's reading.
growth_thesis.claim: Cash generation funds both growth and distributions. Operating cash flow for nine months was 651,755 against 234,051, while cash dividends paid were 581,887 (thousands of dollars). Liquidity was about $964 million. This holds only while operating cash flow stays high; at an at-least-85% payout of adjusted net income, little is retained from earnings.
quotes: Total liquidity was approximately $964 million as of September 30, 2026, including cash and short-term investments of $454 million and $510 million undrawn revolving credit capacity.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q risk factors. The financial impact is not quantified in the evidence.
growth_thesis.claim: Trade-policy conditions are an external requirement for continued growth. U.S. and Chinese port-fee orders on certain vessels are suspended, but no formal extension has been agreed. The company owns 13 China-built vessels and may be subject to the Chinese order. Growth holds only if the suspension is extended or the fees prove manageable.
quotes: The two countries have announced that they expect to extend the suspension of such port fee orders, but to date there has been no formal agreement to do so.

quotes: On November 3, 2026, INSW’s Board of Directors declared a combined dividend of $5.05 per share of common stock payable in the fourth quarter of 2026.

material_events.basis: stated in the Q3 2026 earnings release highlights. The sale date is not printed in the extract.

quotes: Sold a 2012-built Suezmax for proceeds, net of commissions and fees, of $74 million, recognizing a gain of $53 million.

material_events.basis: stated in the Q2 2026 earnings release highlights. The contract date is not printed in the extract.

quotes: Contracted four additional LR1 newbuildings for an aggregate price of $244 million, with deliveries expected in 2028.

risks.basis: Dividend amounts and policy are stated in F3, P7 and P8; the exposure to earnings is inferred.

quotes: Fourth consecutive quarter with a payout ratio of at least 85% of adjusted net income.
INSW may not continue to pay cash dividends on its Common Stock.

risks.basis: Stated in P6; the cost mechanism is inferred.
risks.claim: US and China port fee orders aimed at China-built or Chinese-operated vessels, and at US-controlled owners, are suspended but not formally extended. The company owns 13 China-built vessels.
quotes: On November 10, 2025, the United States and China each suspended its port fee orders for one year.

The United States Trade Representative has proposed to extend the U.S. suspension through January 9, 2027, but the extension has not yet been finalized, and China has not yet formally announced a corresponding extension of its fee suspension.

risks.basis: Stated in P5; the quarterly figures are from F2.

To date, these geopolitical developments have not had a material adverse effect on INSW’s operations, financial condition, results of operations or cash flow.
